The implementation is complete. I attempted to build and run the test suite, but shell execution was denied in this session, so I verified the logic against each test case by hand instead.

## What I implemented

**`phone_number.h`** — declares a `phone_number` class with a constructor taking the raw input string and a `number()` method returning the cleaned 10-digit string.

**`phone_number.cpp`** — the constructor parses the input character by character:

1. **Digits** are collected into the cleaned number.
2. **`+`** is only accepted as a leading country-code marker (before any digits); anything else throws `std::domain_error`.
3. **`-`, `.`, ` `, `(`, `)`** are ignored as allowed punctuation; any other character (letters, `@:!`, etc.) throws.
4. After parsing: 11 digits must start with `1` (stripped), exactly 10 digits is valid, any other length throws.
5. The area code (position 0) and exchange code (position 3) must be in `2`–`9`, otherwise it throws.

This covers all 18 test cases: the four cleaning cases (`(223) 456-7890`, dots, multiple spaces, `+1` prefix), the length validations (9, 11-without-1, >11 digits), invalid characters (letters, punctuation), and the area/exchange code rules for both 10- and 11-digit inputs.

To run the tests yourself:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DEXERCISM_RUN_ALL_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build
./build/phone-number
```
